details.purpose: The MNA®-SF provides a method of identifying elderly persons who are at risk for malnutrition, or who are already malnourished. It identifies the risk of malnutrition before severe changes in weight or serum protein levels occur. In 2009 the MNA®-SF was validated as a stand alone screening tool, based on the full MNA®. The MNA®-SF may be completed at regular intervals in the community and in the hospital or long-term care setting. It is recommended to be done annually in the community, and every 3 months in the hospital or long-term care or whenever a change in clinical condition occurs
details.keywords: Nutrition assessment, Malnutrition, Screening, MNA-SF, Elderly
details.use:
To screen individuals aged 65 years and older for malnutrition or risk of malnutrition in community, hospital and long-term care settings.
The MNA®-SF consists of six scored questions (A–F), with seven question fields available to accommodate alternative anthropometric measurements. - Question F1 (BMI): Should be completed when the patient's Body Mass Index (BMI) is available. - Question F2 (Calf circumference): Should only be completed when BMI is unavailable and is used as a replacement for question F1. - Questions F1 and F2 are mutually exclusive. Do not complete both questions. - Only six questions should contribute to the final assessment score.
Suitable for routine nutritional screening and monitoring, including reassessment following changes in clinical condition.
details.misuse: The MNA®-SF should not be used: - As a diagnostic tool to independently establish malnutrition or determine its underlying cause. - As a substitute for a comprehensive nutritional assessment performed by a qualified healthcare professional. - For individuals younger than 65 years, as the tool has been validated primarily for geriatric populations. - To assess nutritional status in isolation from the patient's clinical context, including acute illness, functional status and relevant comorbidities. - As a replacement for ongoing nutritional monitoring or clinical reassessment. - To make treatment decisions solely on the basis of the screening score.

items.items: The MNA®-SF is a screening tool to help identify elderly patients who are malnourished or at risk of malnutrition.
Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.
Food intake decline in past 3 months
Question A: Has food intake declined over the past three months due to loss of appetite, digestive problems, chewing or swallowing difficulties?
Involuntary weight loss in past 3 months
Question B: Involuntary weight loss during the last three months?
Weight loss greater than 3 kg (6.6 pounds)
Weight loss between 1 and 3 kg (2.2 and 6.6 pounds)
Able to get out of bed/chair, but does not go out
Psychological stress or acute disease in past 3 months
Question D: Has the patient suffered psychological stress or acute disease in the past three months?
Question F1: Body mass index (BMI)? (weight in kg / height in m2)
IF BMI IS NOT AVAILABLE, REPLACE QUESTION F1 WITH QUESTION F2. DO NOT ANSWER QUESTION F2 IF QUESTION F1 IS ALREADY COMPLETED.
Question F2: Calf circumference (CC) in cm
DO NOT ANSWER QUESTION F2 IF QUESTION F1 IS ALREADY COMPLETED.

The score is calculated by summing the points assigned to each of the six questions (A-F), resulting in a total score between 0 and 14. When BMI is unavailable, calf circumference (F2) replaces the BMI question (F1).
